FULL-TIME JOB VACANCY
Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence
Technology, Rights and Investigations Division
Multiple Office Locations Considered
Application Deadline: December 13, 2026
 
Human Rights Watch (HRW) is seeking a highly qualified Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence to investigate, analyze, and advocate against human rights abuses worldwide related to artificial intelligence. The role of the Senior Researcher will include documenting and conveying the rights implications of various forms of artificial intelligence and other algorithmic decision-making being developed and deployed by governments and private sector actors around the world for exclusion and repression, including  information control and censorship and discriminatory decision making, especially in high-risk contexts, for example by law enforcement and immigration authorities. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia is preferred.

The role sits in the Tech and Human Rights team within the broader Technology, Rights and Investigations Division and will report to the Deputy Director based in New York. The Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence will collaborate with other team members in the Technology, Rights and Investigations Division, and colleagues in regional and thematic divisions, and other relevant departments of HRW, including media, legal and policy team, and the advocacy department.

The successful candidate will have deep domain expertise, as well as a track record of conducting research and investigations at the intersection of human rights abuses and AI. The role will be based in any of the following locations where HRW has an office, and will be expected to work from the office on an as-needed basis: New York, Washington DC, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto, Sao Paulo, London, Brussels, Amsterdam, Berlin, Nairobi, Johannesburg, Beirut, or Stockholm. 

Responsibilities:
1. Develop a plan for strategic research and advocacy for influencing the development, application, and regulation of artificial intelligence and similar technologies by governments and the private sector to ensure respect for internationally recognized human rights, including non-discrimination and accountability;
2. Research, document, and analyze policies and practices related to AI, machine learning, and big data technologies that raise human rights concerns by collecting and analyzing information from a wide variety of sources, including governments, media, academia, NGOs, victims of abuses, open-source information, technologists, and others; Interview persons whose rights have been harmed by AI technologies, as well as related professionals and experts (e.g., organizations representing impacted communities, engineers who build AI technologies, data and computer scientists, etc.); 
3. Identify and document where use of AI may have disparate impact on vulnerable or marginalized groups or may exacerbate economic inequality, and place abuses or potential for abuses within the broader political, social and economic contexts;
4. Write and publicize reports, op-eds, press releases, briefing memos, statements, testimony and other materials to disseminate our research findings and policy recommendations for preventing or ending human rights abuses linked to artificial intelligence applications; 
5. Work with colleagues in the Communications Department to develop innovative multimedia and social media strategies to communicate our positions in clear and compelling ways and to advance advocacy;
6. Develop and implement advocacy strategies in collaboration with HRW colleagues to change or prevent abusive government laws, policies, and practices, as well as abusive corporate policies and practices; 
7. Press companies and governments to ensure human rights protections are built into artificial intelligence by design from the outset and articulate how existing human rights standards should apply to emerging AI technologies;  
8. Build partnerships across key communities, including other human rights NGOs, groups representing vulnerable populations, data scientists, machine learning programmers, tech industry leaders, and academics; 
9. Contribute to the shaping of public debates on AI around human rights internationally through clear and prompt responses to queries from policy makers, the media, colleagues, and human rights communities; 
10. Work collaboratively with an international team of researchers within the Technology, Rights and Investigations division, including the Digital Investigations Lab, other thematic and country HRW researchers, and other relevant departments of HRW, including Communications, Legal and Policy, Advocacy, and the General Counsel’s office;
11. Travel domestically and internationally, as required, to conduct research, media work and advocacy; and
12. Be prepared and willing to work flexible hours to accommodate developing and urgent events;
13. Carry out other tasks as required.

Candidate Profile 

Candidates who are traditionally underrepresented in the technology and/or human rights sectors (such as people who identify as BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, women, migrants, people with disabilities, or people who have other related lived experiences) are enthusiastically encouraged to apply if they feel they have the ability to succeed in this role, even if they do not have all the skills and qualifications listed below.

Education: An advanced degree in journalism, law, public policy, national security, computer science, or a related field or equivalent experience is required.

Experience: A minimum of seven years of experience is required. This experience could come from a
variety of previous roles including, but not limited to journalists who have covered technology,
community activism, work at impact litigation organizations, academics, or industry professionals.

Related Skills and Knowledge:
1. Extensive knowledge of artificial intelligence, in particular the threats and complexities it poses to the major human rights challenges of our time is required.
2. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia and fluency in an Asian language are desirable. 
3. Strong commitment to understanding how technology can impact the rights of women, racial and ethnic minorities, children, older people, people with disabilities, people living in poverty and low-wage workers, and other populations whose rights may be disproportionately impacted by AI is desirable.
4. Proven track record of producing timely and high-quality written research and investigations, as well as editing experience is required.
5. Ability to present and defend complex technology-related issues and positions to officials in governments, companies, and other bodies and institutions is preferable.
6. Being comfortable with generating and executing research projects, and the curiosity and creativity to follow through and follow up is required.
7. Exceptionally strong research, analytical, writing, and editing skills are required.
8. Experience conducting challenging investigative research globally is required, as is the ability to dig deep and tenacity in finding hard-to-get information, sources and records.
9. Good oral and written communication skills in English, and strong public speaking skills, are required; proficiency in other languages, is highly desirable.
10. Experience with TV, radio, print, and social media is highly desirable.
11. Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as successfully with a team and across other teams is required.
12. Strong interpersonal skills to work collaboratively within HRW, as well as develop constructive relationships with NGO partners, and company and government officials are required.
13. Demonstrated awareness and sensitivity to the needs and concerns of individuals from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and orientations is required.

Salary and Benefits: HRW offers competitive compensation and employer-paid benefits. HRW offers relocation assistance package and will assist employees in obtaining necessary work authorization in all listed locations except Nairobi, if required; citizens of all nationalities are encouraged to apply. If based in the United States, the salary range would be 88,000 – 104,000. Salary ranges outside of the United States vary based on location.
 
How to Apply: Please apply by December 13, 2026, by visiting our online job portal at careers.hrw.org and submitting a cover letter and CV or resume. No calls or email inquiries, please. Only complete applications will be reviewed and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. 
 
If you are experiencing technical difficulties with your application submission, or if you require disability-related accommodation, please email ----- Rights Watch is strong because it is diverse. We actively seek a diverse applicant pool and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Human Rights Watch does not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or criminal record. We welcome all kinds of diversity. Our employees include people who are parents and nonparents, the self-taught and university educated, and from a wide span of socio-economic backgrounds and perspectives on the world. Human Rights Watch is an equal opportunity employer. 

Human Rights Watch is an international human rights monitoring and advocacy organization known for its in-depth investigations, its incisive and timely reporting, its innovative and high-profile advocacy campaigns, and its success in changing the human rights-related policies and practices of influential governments and international institutions.

descriptionHtml:

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

title: Senior Sales Manager
descriptionHtml:
Du willst Unternehmen zeigen, was KI wirklich für sie tun kann?

Dann komm zu Matelify.

Wir sind ein Startup aus Rödental bei Coburg. Mit Matelify helfen wir Unternehmen, auf Social Media nicht nur zu posten, sondern es zu verstehen. Herzstück sind unsere Mates: fünf KI-Agenten: Cleo erstellt Content, Finn plant, Nova denkt Strategie, Alex analysiert, Max kümmert sich um die Community. Sie arbeiten im Chat live zusammen wie ein eigenes Social-Media-Team.

Jetzt suchen wir dich als Senior Sales Manager in Vollzeit. Jemanden, der Enterprise-Deals gewinnt und unser Sales-Team mit aufbaut.

Was du bei uns machst ⚙️

  • Du gewinnst Enterprise- und Mittelstandskunden, vom ersten Kontakt über Demo und Angebot bis zur Unterschrift.

  • Du verstehst, wie Marketing- und Kommunikationsteams heute arbeiten und zeigst ihnen, wo KI ihnen Zeit spart und bessere Ergebnisse bringt.

  • Du führst Gespräche auf Augenhöhe mit Geschäftsführung, Marketingleitung und Einkauf, auch wenn mehrere Entscheider am Tisch sitzen.

  • Du baust das Sales-Team mit auf: Prozesse, Playbooks, Pipeline und später auch die Leute, die mit dir verkaufen.

  • Du bringst, was du von Kunden hörst, direkt ins Produkt ein. Bei uns sitzt Sales nicht im Silo, sondern am Tisch, wenn wir entscheiden, was wir bauen.

  • Du bist eines der Gesichter von Matelify: auf Events, Messen und überall dort, wo unsere Kunden sind.

Kurz gesagt: Du verkaufst nicht nur ein Produkt, du baust den Vertrieb eines Startups von Grund auf mit.

Wie wir verkaufen 💡

KI-first, auch im Vertrieb. Leads und Termine landen automatisch im CRM. Du arbeitest mit KI-Assistenten, die recherchieren, vorbereiten, nachfassen und hast mehr Zeit für das, was zählt: Gespräche.

Vom Paket bis zur Enterprise-Lösung. Klare Pakete für den schnellen Start und maßgeschneiderte Angebote, wenn ein Kunde mehr braucht.

Kurze Wege. Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Founder-Team. Sonderwünsche klären wir in Minuten, nicht in Wochen.

Hybrid & flexibel: Arbeite dort, wo du am meisten bewegen kannst. Remote mit Fokus, gemeinsam mit dem Team in Rödental oder direkt beim Kunden.

Was du mitbringst ✨

Studium, Ausbildung, Quereinstieg, egal was, es ist uns egal. Uns interessiert, ob du verkaufen kannst, Bock hast und zeigen kannst, was du schon erreicht hast. Wichtig ist uns:

  • Du hast mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb, idealerweise mit Software oder SaaS und hast Deals mit längeren Entscheidungswegen selbst zum Abschluss gebracht.

  • Du weißt, wie Enterprise-Vertrieb läuft: mehrere Ansprechpartner, Einkauf, Freigaben und lässt dich davon nicht aus der Ruhe bringen.

  • Du kennst dich mit KI aus und nutzt sie selbst im Alltag. Du kannst erklären, was sie kann und ehrlich sagen, was nicht.

  • Du hast ein Gefühl für Social Media und Marketing. Du musst kein Profi sein, aber die Sprache deiner Kunden sprechen.

  • Du hast Lust, etwas aufzubauen: Prozesse, die es noch nicht gibt, ein Team, das noch wächst.

  • Du kommunizierst klar und überzeugend und sprichst sehr gut Deutsch und Englisch, mündlich wie schriftlich.

Ein Plus, kein Muss: Erfahrung in einem frühen Startup, ein Netzwerk im Mittelstand oder in Marketingabteilungen, Erfahrung mit dem Aufbau eines Sales-Teams.

Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt? Bewirb dich trotzdem.

Was wir dir bieten 💛

  • Die Chance, den Vertrieb eines wachsenden KI-Startups von Anfang an mitzuprägen

  • Ein Produkt, das man gern zeigt: KI-Agenten, die live zusammenarbeiten, sorgen in jeder Demo für Aha-Momente

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit dem Founder-/CEO-Team

  • Moderner, KI-gestützter Vertrieb statt CRM-Pflege bis Mitternacht

  • Ein kleines, motiviertes Team ohne Politik und Meeting-Marathons

  • Viel Raum für eigene Ideen: die beste Idee gewinnt, nicht die lauteste

  • Hybrides Arbeiten und flexible Arbeitszeiten

So bewirbst du dich 🎬

Schick uns:

  • deinen Lebenslauf oder ein gepflegtes LinkedIn-Profil

  • ein paar Sätze zu dem Deal, auf den du am stolzesten bist

Kein Anschreiben, keine Zeugnisse, kein Notenschnitt. Uns interessiert, wie du denkst und was du schon bewegt hast.

Unser Prozess: kurzes Kennenlernen → Gespräch, in dem du uns Matelify (oder etwas anderes) verkaufst → persönliches Kennenlernen mit dem Team vor Ort in Rödental.

Wir freuen uns auf dich! 🚀

title: Senior Security Architect
descriptionHtml:
Senior Security Architect

Location: London (Hybrid) | Practice Area: Technology & Engineering | Type: Permanent

Shape secure technology architectures and safeguard the digital future of financial services and energy.

The Role

Lead the design of secure, resilient and scalable technology solutions that help financial institutions modernise their platforms, manage evolving cyber threats and deliver complex technology transformation with confidence.

At Capco, you will play a pivotal role in shaping security architecture across some of our clients' most complex and high-profile transformation programmes. Drawing on your expertise in security architecture, cloud technologies and modern security engineering, you will help organisations strengthen their security posture while enabling innovation and business growth.

You will work closely with engineers, architects and senior stakeholders to design practical security solutions, evaluate architectural options and embed security into technology delivery. Your technical judgement, commercial awareness and ability to challenge assumptions constructively will help clients balance security, regulatory compliance, operational resilience and business priorities.

As a Senior Security Architect, you will guide multidisciplinary teams, mentor colleagues and contribute to the development of Capco's Technology & Engineering Practice through technical leadership, knowledge sharing, delivery excellence and business development.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the design and implementation of secure, scalable and resilient architectures across on-premises, cloud and hybrid environments, ensuring solutions align with business objectives, security standards and regulatory requirements.

  • Shape security architecture strategies, technical standards and transformation roadmaps, evaluating architectural options, managing security risks and translating complex requirements into practical, maintainable solutions.

  • Conduct threat modelling, security risk assessments and architectural reviews, defining appropriate security controls and remediation strategies while embedding Zero Trust principles and security-by-design practices.

  • Guide the adoption of DevSecOps practices, integrating security controls throughout the software development lifecycle while collaborating with engineering, architecture and delivery teams to strengthen security outcomes.

  • Explore and apply approved AI tools, automation and AI-enabled workflows to improve security architecture research, threat analysis, design documentation and delivery efficiency, maintaining appropriate human review, security controls, responsible AI governance and clear escalation pathways.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience leading complex security architecture initiatives, translating business, technology and security requirements into practical, high-quality solutions.

  • Strong architectural judgement and problem-solving capability, with the ability to evaluate security risks, challenge assumptions constructively and balance protection, resilience, usability and maintainability.

  • Ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, communicate complex security concepts clearly and influence technology and security decisions across business and engineering teams.

  • Experience working collaboratively across multidisciplinary technical teams, encouraging security awareness, knowledge sharing, engineering excellence and the professional development of colleagues.

  • Commercial awareness and a client-focused mindset, with the ability to understand business objectives, identify opportunities for improvement and deliver measurable security and technology outcomes.

Technical Skills & Experience

Essential Requirements

  • Security architecture across on-premises, cloud and hybrid environments: Proven experience designing and implementing secure architectures across complex technology estates, including cloud infrastructure, hybrid platforms and enterprise systems.

  • Security technologies and ecosystems: Experience designing solutions using Palo Alto, Microsoft or comparable security ecosystems, with a strong understanding of security architecture principles and their practical application.

  • Security frameworks and Zero Trust Architecture: Deep knowledge of recognised security frameworks and standards, including NIST, ISO 27001, CAF and TOGAF, combined with experience designing and implementing Zero Trust Architecture solutions.

  • Security engineering and risk management: Strong expertise across Identity and Access Management (IAM), endpoint protection, application security and network security, including threat modelling, security risk assessments and the definition of appropriate remediation strategies.

  • DevSecOps and secure delivery: Experience embedding security controls into the software development lifecycle, applying DevSecOps principles and collaborating with engineering teams to support secure software and infrastructure delivery.

Bonus Points For

  • Relevant professional certifications, including CISSP, CISM, TOGAF or recognised cloud security certifications.

  • Experience defining AI security architectures, responsible AI governance frameworks, security guardrails or controls for AI-enabled systems, including Generative AI and Agentic AI, within regulated environments.

  • Hands-on experience with security tooling, including Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms, firewalls and Identity and Access Management solutions.

  • Experience supporting regulatory compliance requirements, including GDPR and PCI-DSS, particularly within financial services or other regulated industries.

  • Familiarity with programming languages such as Python, Java or C++, with the ability to understand how software engineering practices influence security architecture and technical delivery.

Why Join Capco

  • Deliver high-impact technology solutions for Tier 1 financial institutions.

  • Work in a collaborative, flat and entrepreneurial consulting culture.

  • Access continuous learning, training and industry certifications.

  • Be part of a team shaping the future of digital financial services.

  • Help shape the future of digital transformation across financial services and energy.

Benefits

We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life:

  • Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover.

  • Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders.

  • Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement.

  • Family Care: 8 complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care.

  • Holiday Flexibility: 5 weeks of annual leave with the option to buy or sell holiday days based on your needs.

  • Continuous Learning: Your growth, your way – a minimum of 40 hours of training annually. Take your pick from workshops, certifications and e-learning. You'll also be assigned a Business Coach from Day One, offering one-on-one guidance to support your goals and accelerate your development.

  • Healthcare Access: Convenient online GP services.

  • Extra Perks: Gympass (Wellhub), travel insurance, Tastecard, season ticket loans, Cycle to Work, and dental insurance.

Inclusion at Capco

We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know – we’ll be happy to help. We value each person’s unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration – a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day.

  • Experience with streaming data, event systems, real-time processing, or low-latency applications.

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

WHY CATAPULT?

That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve. There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

title: Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
descriptionHtml:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product.

You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own.

You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another.

🧩 The problem you would be working on

Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence.

OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost.

Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one.

OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable.

🛠️ What you would work on

  • End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome.

  • The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability.

  • The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.

  • Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.

  • The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.

🏆 What success could look like

Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:

  • Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.

  • Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.

  • Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.

  • Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.

  • Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.

  • Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.

🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran

OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.

👥 The squad

You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.

You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.

✨ What will help you succeed

We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.

  • A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.

  • Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.

  • The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.

  • Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.

  • Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.

  • Fluent English is required.

💡 Useful, but not required

Any of the following would help, but none is expected:

  • Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.

  • Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.

  • Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.

⚙️ The stack

TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.

OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling.

A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.

💰 What you can expect

  • Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success

  • 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work

  • Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you

  • Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen

🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. title: Senior Strategic Solutions Consultant (AI)
descriptionHtml:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

You will work with our most strategic customers, understand their strategy and key challenges, and build Celonis solutions using cutting-edge AI technologies from market leaders such as Microsoft and OpenAI. With Celonis’ market-leading Process Intelligence (PI) Platform we feed operational context to AI so it understands our customers’ businesses and enables them to industrialize AI unlocking real ROI on AI deployments and at scale. There is no AI without PI. You will prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption and value realization to increase Celonis' footprint at those customers.

The Role:

As Senior Applied Value Engineer, you are a strategic pioneer leading the charge in solving complex, business-critical problems for our customers. Working with our most strategic global accounts, you will diagnose their strategy and key operational challenges to discover and build tailored, domain-specific use cases. You will architect and prototype state-of-the-art AI and technical solutions on the Celonis platform, demonstrate their business impact to C-suite Executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realization. 

Native-level German proficiency (C1/C2) is required for this role. Candidates must be able to lead customer workshops, conduct executive presentations, and manage stakeholder interactions in German.

The work you’ll do:

Seamlessly translate deep domain expertise and complex customer requirements into flawless enterprise architecture. You will lead technical discovery to architect, prototype, and build bespoke, state-of-the-art AI solutions targeting nuanced operational pain points.
  • AI Solution Development: Lead the end-to-end execution of high-stakes Proof-of-Value (PoV) projects. Architect and deliver highly secure, scalable LLM/agent systems with advanced RAG, tools, and strict guardrails; integrating flawlessly with rigid enterprise data, identity, and compliance frameworks.

title: Senior Talent Partner, Tech
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Why this role exists

 

We are about to hire the people who will define the next phase of this company. Not backfill a plan someone else wrote — define it. The quality of who joins Dust over the next eighteen months is the single highest-leverage variable in whether we build the category or watch someone else do it.

 

That work needs a recruiter who treats hiring as a craft rather than a queue. Someone who can hold a real point of view on what "great" looks like for a role, defend it with a hiring manager who disagrees, and then go find that person themselves — from a cold start, without a lead gen team, a sourcing pod, or a playbook waiting for them.

 

You'll be an early member of a small Talent team. That means you own roles end to end, and you also help build the thing itself: the assessment design, the interview loops, the calibration, the data we use to know whether any of it is working.

 

We're looking for someone who cares about the candidate experience for all parties internal and external. And prioritizes protecting Dust's culture by being thoughtful, thorough and leading by example in being a true team player.

  

What you'll own

 

Full-cycle hiring, end to end. You run your own searches from role kickoff to close. Sourcing, outreach, screening, interviewing, offer strategy, negotiation. You are the owner of the outcome, not a coordinator of other people's opinions.

 

Assessment design, not just assessment delivery. For every role you open, you help define what evidence would actually predict success — then you build the loop that surfaces it. You'll push back on interview stages that exist out of habit and replace them with ones that test something real.

 

Hiring manager partnership with a spine. You'll spend as much time calibrating hiring managers as you do talking to candidates. When a manager says "not quite the right feel," you'll ask what they mean until there's a defensible answer, and you'll say so when there isn't one.

 

Market intelligence. You'll know your talent market better than anyone else in the building — who's good, where they are, what moves them, what compensation actually looks like right now — and you'll bring that back into how we scope roles and design offers.

 

The candidate experience. Our hiring process is the first honest sample of what working here feels like. You'll make it expedient, direct, well-communicated, and worth a candidate's time whether or not they get an offer.

 

Building the function. Process, tooling, structured scorecards, funnel data, quality-of-hire signal. You'll leave the system better than you found it, and you'll be trusted to change it without asking permission first.

  

Two tracks — tell us which one is yours

 

We're hiring for depth in one of two areas. You should have a genuine centre of gravity in one; interest in the other is a bonus, not a requirement.

 

GTM. Account Executives, Sales Engineers, Customer Success, Marketing, and the leaders above them, across Europe and the US. You know how to assess commercial talent on evidence rather than swagger, and you can tell the difference between a rep who carried a territory and a rep who inherited one.

 

Technical. Software engineers, infrastructure, product, and design, in a market where the best people are not looking and the second-best are drowning in outreach. You can hold a credible conversation about what someone actually built, and you know why that matters more than where they built it.

  

How we think about hiring

 

We're telling you this up front because if you disagree with it, this will be a frustrating job.

 

  • We don't hire based on pedigree. Logos and school names are weak evidence. What someone has actually done, and what they can demonstrate now, is strong evidence. We design our loops accordingly.

  • We hire for evidence, not affinity. "Culture fit" that means "reminds me of me" is how companies get homogeneous and slow. We assess against explicit behaviours tied to how we work, and we write down what we saw.

  • Speed and rigour are not in tension. Slow processes are usually a symptom of unclear thinking about the role, not of high standards.

  • A no should be as clear as a yes. To the candidate, and internally.

  • Some of us came from well-known companies. That's context, not criteria. It isn't why we're here and it won't be why you are. We celebrate everyone's achievements and want to create an environment where diversity of thought and experience of a collective whole makes this place exceptional and lasting.

  • Recruiters are operators, not order-takers. If you think a role is wrongly scoped, badly levelled, or shouldn't be open at all, you're expected to say so.

  

What we're looking for

 

  • 5+ years in full-cycle recruiting, with meaningful time in-house at a high-growth company. You've hired in an environment with real ambiguity, not just real volume.

  • Demonstrable depth in either GTM or technical hiring — you can talk through searches you've run, what made them hard, and what you'd do differently.

  • Genuinely strong sourcing. Not "I partner with a sourcing team." You find people yourself, and you write outreach that people reply to because it's obviously written by a human who read something.

  • Comfort operating without infrastructure. No playbook, no SDR equivalent, limited tooling to start.

  • The judgement and directness to challenge senior stakeholders, and the credibility to be listened to when you do.

  • A bias to start. You see the gap and close it before anyone asks you to.

  • Excellent written English and a real feel for language. Everything you write is a piece of our employer brand.

  • Low ego, high ownership. No job is too big or too small — you'll design an assessment framework in the morning and chase a scheduling conflict in the afternoon.

  • Based in Paris, London or New York.

 

Ideal, but not required: experience hiring in AI or developer-facing companies; experience building or improving a hiring process rather than inheriting one; multi-market hiring across Europe and the US.

  

You'll be using AI to do this job — properly

 

We build the AI operating system that companies use to rewire their work. We expect our own team to be the sharpest possible example of that.

 

You'll build and run your own Dust agents: market maps, candidate research, interview debrief synthesis, competitive intelligence on where talent is moving. Not as a side project — as how the job gets done. You don't need to have done this before, but you do need to be the kind of person who is genuinely excited to, rather than politely tolerant of it.

 

You'll also be one of our most credible internal sources of feedback on the product, because you'll be a heavy user of it every day.

  

Location

 

This role is based in Paris, London or New York, and we'd love you to spend real time in the office with the team. A lot of the best things about building at Dust happen because people are in the same room: the energy, the fast decisions, the unexpected conversation that unlocks a hard problem.

 

We hire people with strong judgement and extend that trust to how they manage their time.

  

Our process

 

We'll tell you the full loop up front, keep it to a small number of stages, and give you a decision quickly. You'll meet the people you'd work with, not a panel of proxies. Expect at least one stage where you work through a real hiring problem with us rather than describing a past one.

 

If you don't check every box, apply anyway. We're more interested in your potential and how you think than a perfect match to a checklist.

 

Please send your application and resume in English.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Senior Technical Sales Manager - AI-Driven Software Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About CREATEQ

CREATEQ is a Swiss software engineering company with more than 30 years of experience in delivering custom software solutions and modernizing complex legacy systems. We work with leading international companies across industries such as banking and fintech, insurance, aviation and transportation, telecommunications, and energy.

We design, build, and run high-quality software solutions, combining strong engineering expertise, modern technologies, AI-enabled approaches, and proven delivery practices. Our teams work across Java, .NET, PHP, mobile, and web development, helping clients modernize their technology landscapes, improve their software capabilities, and build solutions that are reliable, scalable, and ready for the future.

We are fully dedicated to long-term partnerships, working as one organization with our customers and taking ownership from the first idea through to reliable execution and smooth operation. With nearshore delivery centers across Europe, we bring together experienced engineering and delivery teams who combine technical excellence, business understanding, and a strong sense of ownership.

People, engineering excellence, and strong client relationships are at the heart of what we do.

The opportunity

We are looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial Senior Technical Sales Manager to drive new business for CREATEQ with full revenue responsibility. In this role, you will win new clients, shape their entry into AI-driven software engineering, and turn it into long-term engineering engagements delivered by our teams.

Many companies still develop software the traditional way, mostly on Java and .NET. They want to benefit from AI-driven development but lack the know-how, processes, and capacity to do so. This is where you come in: you understand the client's starting point, develop the right approach together with them – from assessment and proof of concept to dedicated nearshore teams – and close the deal.

You will work closely with management, Business Development, and our engineering leads, and you will be the face of CREATEQ to CIOs, CTOs, and Heads of Engineering in Switzerland [and the DACH region].

What you'll do

  • Build and close your own pipeline with mid-sized and large companies in Switzerland [and the DACH region].
  • Assess clients' development processes, technology stacks, and AI maturity, and run workshops with engineering teams, IT leadership, and executive management.
  • Develop solution concepts and proposals – from assessment and proof of concept to dedicated nearshore engineering teams.
  • Lead commercial negotiations through to contract signature.
  • Grow existing client relationships and secure follow-on business.
  • Work closely with our engineering leads on team set-up, project kick-off, and quality assurance.
  • Track pipeline, order intake, and revenue against agreed targets and report on progress to management.

What we're looking for

This is a senior role with clear revenue responsibility. We are looking for someone who has successfully sold IT services before, brings a strong network in the Swiss market, and is equally credible in conversations with developers and with executive management.

Requirements

  • At least 8 years of experience selling IT services, software engineering, or nearshore/offshore capacity, including several years with personal revenue responsibility.
  • A proven track record in acquiring new clients and closing multi-year service engagements.
  • A strong network among CIOs, CTOs, and Heads of Engineering in the Swiss market.
  • A technical background (computer science, business informatics, or equivalent practical experience) with a solid understanding of Java and/or .NET environments and modern engineering practices (CI/CD, automated testing, DevOps).
  • A solid understanding of AI-driven software development (AI coding assistants, agentic development tools) and a realistic view of its benefits and limitations.
  • An entrepreneurial, closing-oriented mindset and the ability to work independently.
  • Native/Fluent German and excellent written and spoken English.
  • Swiss or EU citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit.

Benefits

  • A key role with direct impact on CREATEQ's growth.
  • An offering that is high on clients' agendas: AI-driven software engineering, delivered by experienced engineering teams.
  • A compensation package with a fixed salary and a performance-based component.
  • Direct collaboration with management and short decision paths.
  • Freedom to shape the role, bring your ideas, and make a visible impact.
  • A long-term perspective in an international software engineering company with a strong presence in the European market.

This understanding includes but is not exhaustive to Treasury investment securities, derivative instruments (interest rate swaps and FX forwards), hedge accounting and financial reporting.

We have some really exciting challenges coming up like continued expansion into the European Union, growing our customer base, keep growing our lending business and adding to our marketplace. This all leads to exciting Treasury activity to support this growth whilst managing risk. You’ll work on scaling Monzo in a controlled way, while helping us optimise our financial control processes with the help of technology. You’ll join the Finance team and report to our Head of Treasury Product Control. 

🔑  You’ll play a key role by…

  • Working very closely with our Treasury front office, treasury operations and financial control teams as we continue to build our treasury product control capabilities in Finance.
  • Taking ownership of the end-to-end control processes on Treasury products. This includes:
    • Independent trade confirmation for all Treasury deals booked in our Treasury Management System (TMS)
    • Daily collateral management for our derivative and REPO portfolios 
    • Daily profit and loss reporting on Treasury income to CFO/Treasuer
    • Valuation controls around Treasury financial instrument pricing
  • Managing Treasury month-end processes, including derivatives and hedge accounting. 
  • Maintaining existing and developing new treasury related internal controls that protect our financial data and our balance sheet substantiation process, working with 2LoD and 3LoD along the way.
  • Supporting our year end processes, preparing Treasury related disclosures, dealing with external audit queries and ad hoc assistance on non-Treasury related aspects of the cycle. 
  • Understanding the Treasury business and their products to write insightful management commentary on results.
  • Reviewing new Treasury products, assessing and determining the accounting treatment before implementing the GL configuration mapping in our TMS.
  • Working with our engineers and data teams to automate the production elements of this role, allowing you to focus on the parts of the role where your knowledge and skills provide the most value.
  • Learning SQL skills to run reports and propose solutions that make our processes efficient and scalable.
  • Ad hoc support on non-Treasury related initiatives.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if you..

  • You’re a qualified accountant and have knowledge and/or understanding of Treasury products in a banking context.
  • You have a great eye for detail and a thirst to learn, which sees you develop into the subject matter for all things Treasury.
  • You’re fascinated by the banking and regulatory landscape, and have a good understanding of key internal controls.
  • You’re a self-starter and enjoy tackling what needs doing, whether it’s confirming trade accuracy or pulling together complex disclosures in a simplified way for derivatives in our annual report.
  • You’re comfortable translating complex information into simple words for people with diverse backgrounds.
  • You’re interested in using data (SQL skills would be a bonus).
  • You thrive in a dynamic and constantly evolving environment.
  • What we’re doing at Monzo excites you!

🙌 What’s in it for you

  • 💰 £56,100 - £75,900 (depending on experience) + Incentive Award tied to your performance. 
  • 📍This role can be based in our London or Cardiff offices. We're also open to distributed working within the UK (with the expectation of some travel to our London office).
  • ⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team.
  • 📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.
  • 🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

This process should take around 3 - 4 weeks, your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!

title: Senior Underwriter - Bridging
descriptionHtml:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

The Bridging Department at Allica Bank is a high-energy, specialist lending team supporting established SMEs and professional property investors with fast, flexible short-term finance. Operating within a true challenger-bank environment, the team combines strong credit discipline with pragmatic decision-making, relationship-led lending, and a clear focus on delivering the right outcomes for customers.

This is a fast-paced and constantly evolving department where no two days are the same. Deals are time-critical, varied, and often bespoke, requiring commercial thinking, sound judgement, and a willingness to take ownership from day one. As the Bridging proposition continues to grow, the role and the department evolve week by week offering genuine variety, exposure, and the opportunity to help shape how the business operates.

The team is lively, proactive, and highly collaborative. People are trusted to act like owners, take responsibility for their decisions, and work closely with colleagues across Distribution, Credit, Operations, and external partners to keep things moving. There is a strong emphasis on keeping things clear and simple, working at pace, and removing unnecessary barriers to getting good deals done without compromising on risk or governance.

Role Description

The purpose of this role is to underwrite larger and more complex borrowing requests across Allica Bank’s Bridging proposition, received via a variety of origination channels. The Senior Underwriter will assess and structure lending proposals in line with the Bank’s approved Credit Policy, risk appetite, and asset strategy, while supporting the delivery of fast, high-quality outcomes for SME and professional property clients.

The role covers a broad range of asset classes within the Bank’s portfolio, including (but not limited to) residential investment properties, commercial and semi-commercial assets, and refurbishment transactions involving staged drawdowns.

Senior Underwriters are expected to hold a Delegated Lending Authority mandate and to provide oversight and recommendations on approvals, policy exceptions, and escalated cases, including appeals, within their delegated authority. In addition, Senior Underwriters will act as a signatory for cases falling within lower lending mandates.

Underwriters take full ownership of each deal from initial application through to completion. This includes managing and responding to all underwriting and legal requisitions, working closely with brokers, solicitors, valuers, intermediaries, and internal stakeholders to resolve issues efficiently and progress transactions.

As a senior member of the team, the role contributes to the ongoing development of the Bridging proposition, working closely with Relationship Management, Credit Risk, Operations, and other stakeholders to continuously refine processes, appetite, and ways of working in line with Allica’s challenger-bank culture.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Assess and underwrite larger and more complex credit applications within personal delegated authority, in line with all regulatory requirements, the Bank’s credit appetite, and approved underwriting policies, utilising appropriate credit data, financial analysis, and risk assessment tools

  • Produce clear, accurate, and concise written credit papers, providing well-reasoned recommendations to the Credit team for applications falling outside personal discretion or credit policy, and escalating cases as required to the appropriate Delegated Lending Authorities

  • Undertake regular control checks and ongoing monitoring to ensure the Bank’s risk management, governance, and customer information requirements are always met, escalating immediately any identified issues, breaches, or areas of concern

  • Manage and take full ownership of the end-to-end application process, from initial application through to completion, liaising effectively with brokers, valuers, asset managers, solicitors, and internal stakeholders to ensure appropriate security is in place and all lending is fully documented prior to drawdown.

  • Work closely with the wider team to support effective management of the overall credit risk environment, including portfolio performance, concentration risk, and the ongoing development and refinement of credit policy

  • Liaise effectively with applicants, brokers, valuers, and other third parties to obtain additional information required to support robust and timely credit decision-making

  • Deliver an excellent level of service to customers, brokers, and Relationship Managers, building and maintaining strong, professional relationships in line with the Bank’s values and customer experience standards

  • Ensure full compliance with all mandatory policies, regulatory requirements, and credit procedures, always maintaining strong internal controls and governance

  • Where applicable, complete monthly assurance and quality assurance dip-testing on cases agreed for direct reports, providing clear feedback, guidance, and development support as required.

Personal Attributes & Experience

  • A highly accomplished underwriter with strong experience in manual underwriting within the Bridging sector, demonstrating a deep understanding of the competitive landscape, market dynamics, and evolving trends in short-term property finance

  • Strong credit and financial analysis capability, including the assessment of financial accounts, budgets, and cashflow forecasts, with the confidence to apply sound commercial judgement, make balanced risk decisions within personal discretion

  • Proven experience of confidently escalating complex cases and presenting at Credit Committee, demonstrating accountability, clarity of thought, and ownership of decisions

  • Clear, confident communicator with strong analytical, verbal, and written skills, able to explain risk, structure, and rationale effectively to a wide range of stakeholders

  • Highly organised with excellent time-management and prioritisation skills, able to thrive in a fast-paced, changeable environment

  • A collaborative team player who builds strong, trusted relationships across Distribution, Operations, Credit, and senior management, as well as with external partners including intermediaries, valuers, and solicitors

  • Demonstrates a strong commitment to doing the right thing for customers and the Bank, with a thorough understanding of regulatory requirements, internal policies, procedures, risk controls, and service level expectations

  • Flexible, adaptable, and responsive to business needs, willing to adjust priorities and ways of working to meet SLAs and deliver excellent customer and broker outcomes

  • Established working knowledge of Treating Customers Fairly (TCF), Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Know Your Customer (KYC), and Conduct Risk

  • Confident user of technology, with experience of CRM systems and strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word to support effective analysis, reporting, and decision-making

    #LI-AD1

Working at Allica Bank

At Allica Bank we want to ensure our employees have the right tools and environment in which to succeed in their role and in support of our customers.

Our employees are at the heart of everything we do, so our benefits are designed with you in mind:

  • Full onboarding support and continued development opportunities

  • Options for flexible working

  • Regular social activities

  • Pension contributions

  • Discretionary bonus scheme

  • Private health cover

  • Life assurance

  • Family friendly policies including enhanced Maternity & Paternity leave

Don’t tick every box?

Don’t worry if you don’t have all the skills or requirements listed on the job description. If you think you’ll be a good fit, we’d still love to hear from you!

Flexible working

We know the ‘9-to-5’ isn’t right for everyone. That’s why Allica Bank is fully committed to flexible and hybrid working. Please let us know what is best for you and, if we can, we will do our best to accommodate.

Diversity

We’re a diverse bunch here at Allica, with all kinds of experiences, backgrounds and lifestyles. Our openness and differences make us stronger, and we want everybody to feel comfortable bringing as much of themselves to work with them as they like.

AI-assisted engineering is part of our daily toolchain because it materially improves how we build and operate the platform – from spec-driven development with LLM assistance and knowledge-base-driven retrieval for incident response and design to agentic coding workflows and faster runbook authoring and review. title: Software Engineer, Data
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Engelhart was founded in 2013 by BTG Pactual Group as a commodities trading company. Our business model is “asset light” and highly diversified – giving us the ability to adapt effectively and nimbly to changing market conditions. We have assembled successful multidisciplinary teams, leveraging advanced fundamental analysis with deep quantitative and weather research capabilities.  Our activities are underpinned by strong risk management practices and by powerful technology and operational excellence. We have exceptional teams with diverse global backgrounds and decades of experience, and are driven by a highly collaborative culture, across products and competencies.

In 2024, Engelhart acquired Trailstone, a global energy trading and technology company. The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. The acquisition also expanded Engelhart’s capabilities into physical natural gas across North America, a critical fuel to support the energy transition.

Our talented and experienced individuals work together according to its four company values: Performance, Agility, Collaboration, Entrepreneurship.

About the Role

As a member of the Data team, you will help build the services, infrastructure, and data platforms that power our business. Our team is responsible for ingesting, processing, storing, and distributing large volumes of data reliably and efficiently, enabling teams across the business to make data-driven decisions and build innovative products.  

This role sits at the intersection of backend software engineering and data engineering, with an emphasis on data engineering. You will build and maintain data pipelines, develop backend services for data ingestion and access, and contribute to the data infrastructure that enables reliable, cost-effective, and high-performance data processing. 

You'll work closely with software engineers, DevOps engineers, product managers, data consumers, and more experienced colleagues, who will provide guidance, code reviews, and support as you grow. While the role involves technical collaboration across the organization, it is primarily focused on engineering rather than stakeholder management. 

We are a trading company, so business requirements change quickly, and priorities can shift. We are looking for someone who enjoys solving technical problems, takes ownership of their work, is eager to learn, and makes pragmatic engineering decisions in a dynamic environment. 

Responsibilities 

  • Build and maintain reliable data pipelines and ingestion workflows for structured and unstructured data from a variety of internal and external sources, including fetching data from external providers.
  • Develop and maintain backend services and APIs (e.g., FastAPI) that support data ingestion, processing, and distribution, including asynchronous ingestion at scale.
  • Transform and process data using Python and Pandas.
  • Contribute to reusable frameworks and tooling that simplify onboarding new data sources and improve developer productivity.
  • Work with data lakes, analytical and relational databases, and contribute to their design and optimization together with senior colleagues.
  • Help catalogue and document the data we own so it can be discovered and used by others.
  • Help improve the reliability, scalability, observability, and cost-efficiency of our data infrastructure.
  • Integrate data across multiple systems while reducing duplication and ensuring high data quality.
  • Contribute to orchestration workflows and automated data processing pipelines.
  • Build internal libraries and services that enable other engineering teams to access and consume data efficiently.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and fix issues in production systems and data pipelines, escalating when needed.
  • Participate in architecture discussions and technical decisions across the data platform.
  • Collaborate with software engineers, DevOps engineers, product managers, and data consumers to deliver high-impact solutions.
  • Build and maintain simple internal self-service tools, occasionally including a user interface.
  • Use AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot) responsibly to speed up development, while remaining accountable for the design, correctness, and quality of your code.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify systems, improve automation, and reduce operational overhead. 

About You 

The following education, experience, and skills are essential for this role: 

  • Background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Around 2+ years of professional experience in data engineering or backend development, with a focus on data pipelines and data-intensive systems.
  • Professional experience developing applications and services using Python, including data processing with Pandas or similar libraries.
  • Experience building or working with data pipelines (ETL/ELT) or data processing systems.

Strong software engineering skills are essential; the role involves little manual testing.

title: Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.

Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

How we work

  • Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.

  • Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

  • At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

  • End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

  • In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.

  • Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

  • Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

  • Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

  • AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

  • Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

What we look for

  • A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

  • Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

  • High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

  • Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

  • Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.
